newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Randfontein reported weighing big job cuts.
newsitem.headline: Randfontein reported weighing big job cuts.

text.p: South African mining house JCI Ltd was on Tuesday reported to be weighing heavy job cuts at its Randfontein Estates Gold Mining Co Ltd.

Local papers quoted the National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) as saying the company had advised unions and associations of possible restructuring in the wake of poor March quarter gold results, reported last month.
The local Business Report said the mine may retrench as many as 8,000 of its current 12,000 workforce, while the Business Day newspaper said the mine was considering cutting 4,000 jobs.

JCI spokesman Mark Gonsalves confirmed that discussions were taking place with the respective unions and associations and said an announcement on the number of jobs to go would be made this week, the Business Day said.
The weak bullion price, declining ore grades and management problems were also cited as responsible for threatening jobs.
NUM spokesman Thabani Mngomezulu was quoted by the Business Report as saying retrenchments had already begun and that workers had lost faith in newly-appointed JCI chairman Mzi Khumalo.

Randfontein produced 4,392 kg of gold in the March quarter compared to 5,100 kg in the December quarter. It plunged into a loss of 2.86 million rand, well down on the previous quarter's 43.83 million rand profit.
At the time of reporting the March quarter the mine announced that these results could lead to a further labour retructuring programme.
